en: Vimānavatthu: The Chapter on the Woman’s Vimānas,
Section on the Seats (Pīṭhavagga)
12. The Second Mansion of the Faithful Wife "Having ascended this many-colored mansion, resplendent and radiant with pillars of beryl,"
There you dwell, O goddess of great majesty,
manifesting various high and low supernatural powers;
and these nymphs surround you on every side.
They dance, sing, and bring delight.
Having attained divine power, O lady of great majesty,
what merit did you perform while you were a human being?
“By what means have you become so radiant in power, and why does your complexion illuminate all directions?
The deity, being delighted, [replied:]
Questioned by Moggallāna,
she answered the question asked,
[explaining] the fruit of that karma.
“Among humans, having been born as a human,
I was a female lay follower of the One with Vision;
I abstained from taking life.”
In this world, I shall avoid taking what is not given.
I shall drink no intoxicants and speak no falsehoods;
I shall be content with my own husband.
With a mind full of faith, I gave abundant gifts of food and drink with due respect;
by that, such is my complexion.
By that, I succeed here;
and whatever riches arise that are dear to my mind, they come to me.
I tell you, O monk of great power,
that while still human beings we performed meritorious deeds;
because of that, we possess such blazing majesty.
"And my radiance shines in all directions.
Thus ends the twelfth Vimāna, the Second on the Faithful Wife.
